rubric.statement: ReAct synthesizes a new `react_signature` rather than reusing the task signature directly: it carries over the original input fields, prepends `signature.instructions` when present, and adds `trajectory` as an extra string input.

The synthesized instructions append fixed agent guidance that says the model is an Agent, sees the original input fields plus past trajectory, must use supplied tools to gather information for the original outputs, interleave `next_thought`, `next_tool_name`, and `next_tool_args` on every turn including finish, and receives an observation after each tool call.
ReAct injects a synthetic `finish` tool with name `finish`, empty `args`, and a description that marks the task complete once information for the original outputs is available.
The instruction block enumerates every tool as numbered lines, and each line comes from `Tool.__str__`, which prints the tool name, description, and `args` schema derived for that tool.
The output contract constrains `next_tool_name` to `Literal[tuple(tools.keys())]`, so the only valid tool names are the registered tools after `finish` has been added.

The contract explicitly says `next_tool_args` must be JSON and types it as `dict[str, Any]`; the Pydantic-args test exercises a nested dict in `next_tool_args` for the tool call and `{}` for `finish`.
